examples.target: My company is considering making remote work permanent. What is your opinion?
But does productivity not suffer when people are at home?
I am in favor, mainly because of the flexibility it gives employees.
And what about isolation? I miss chatting with colleagues at the coffee machine.
The commute is the worst part, I must admit. I lose two hours a day.
So the question is how to balance work and private life.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: My company is considering making remote work permanent. What is your opinion?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I am in favor, mainly because of the flexibility it gives employees.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: But does productivity not suffer when people are at home?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Studies suggest the opposite for many jobs, though it depends on the person.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: I find it hard to concentrate at home, with all the distractions.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That is a fair point. A proper workspace makes a big difference.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: And what about isolation? I miss chatting with colleagues at the coffee machine.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Me too, to be honest. That is why I think a hybrid model works best.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: Two or three days in the office, perhaps?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Exactly. You keep the human contact and still avoid the daily commute.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: The commute is the worst part, I must admit. I lose two hours a day.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Imagine what you could do with that time: sport, family, sleep.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: It is also better for the environment, of course.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: True, although heating a home all day uses energy, too.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: So the question is how to balance work and private life.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Right. Clear working hours are essential, otherwise you never really switch off.
